Persistent systemd journal, Journal window around each soft-reboot, Swap and hibernation, NixOS account bookkeeping, The hidden session's /run carried into the decoy, An interrupted entry's runtime files in /run, Hidden kernel records imported by the decoy journal, Memory remanence (live host only)
Classic syslog daemon, Shell history, Desktop recent-files lists (re-run with --deep)
Decoy journal reset by the way back: RAM only, gone at power-off
Armed kdump: the crash-dumps row probes /var/crash, where kdump writes its dumps
Decoy filesystems the hidden systemd would mount: verify cannot tell what a session wrote to another filesystem
Disks mounted during the hidden session: verify cannot tell what a session wrote to another disk
Network state the hidden session created or changed: a link the decoy adopted looks like one the decoy made itself
Soft-reboot counter and boot ID: RAM only, gone at power-off
Login and boot records around a switch: the records are the decoy's own; verify reports the pieces the way back leaves in /run when their step never ran
The decoy's mounts made again by the way back: RAM only, gone at power-off
EFI NVRAM, RTC and firmware pstore: EFI variables and firmware storage are not part of a disk image
SMART power-on hours: a disk image does not carry SMART counters
SSD flash-translation-layer remnants: no host-side read reaches remapped flash cells, so `nails rehearse` cannot see them either
NetworkManager connection records: a connection record the decoy wrote after adopting a session's link looks like one the decoy made itself

Copy-on-write and compressed storage history: a raw scan reads old copy-on-write extents but cannot read compressed ones, so `nails rehearse` reports a compressed or copy-on-write decoy as not checked rather than clean: a mounted one (a zfs dataset included) by its mount, an image or an unmounted device by its superblock, and a whole disk partition by partition, where an encrypted partition, or one on which no filesystem is identified, is not checked either

Pending offline update: a link staged on the decoy is on the decoy disk, where a scan sees it, but it is the decoy's own state, not a trace of a session; a link a session staged sits in the upper on the hidden volume, where the next activation finds it and refuses

sssd and the domain controller's records: the domain controller keeps its records on the controller, out of reach of any scan of this computer; what a scan of the decoy disk sees of sssd is the decoy's own, its caches under /var/lib/sss and the lines it logs under /var/log/sssd when it stops before the switch and starts after the way back, as at any shutdown and boot
